types.name: Statement and conclusions
types.description: A statement or situation is followed by conclusions I and II, and you decide which conclusion logically follows from it.

types.name: Statement and assumptions
types.description: A statement is followed by assumptions, and you decide which are implicit, that is, taken for granted by the speaker.

types.name: Courses of action
types.description: A problem or situation is followed by courses of action I and II, and you decide which ones should be pursued.

types.name: Cause and effect
types.description: Two events are given (or a statement with possible reasons), and you decide which is the cause, which is the effect, or whether they share a common cause.

types.name: Statement and arguments
types.description: A question such as "Should X be done?" is followed by "Yes" and "No" arguments, and you decide which arguments are strong.

types.name: Statement and inferences
types.description: A statement or short passage is followed by inferences, or asks "which of the following can be inferred", and you pick what is true or most likely true.

types.name: Data sufficiency
types.description: A question is followed by two statements I and II, and you decide whether one, either, both together or neither is enough to answer it, without fully solving it.

types.name: Inequality statements
types.description: Letters are joined by signs such as >, <, ≥, ≤, = (or coded symbols standing for them), and you check which conclusions are definitely true.
